transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kulkarni (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Verdant Head of Partnerships), Elena Park (Verdant Dir Solutions), Ravi Singh (Verdant SE)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood Inference and Verdant GPU Systems — discuss reseller/partner model, integration points for private deployments, benchmarking for Dedicated offerings, and co-marketing. Agreed to run a benchmark and follow up with technical deep dive.

Topics:
- Partnership model (reseller vs referral vs integration)
- Technical integration (VPC, Private deployment, KMS/HSM, SOC2)
- Supported GPU SKUs and quantization/TF32/FP16 tradeoffs
- Initial benchmark scope and timelines
- Go-to-market and co-sell motions

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the partnership side, we've got Priya here from our se team, uh do you want to do quick intros?
00:09 Marco Diaz: yeah hi Marco here at Verdant, i run partnerships, we focus on enterprise-grade gpu hosting, uh primarily in eu and na currently
00:15 Elena Park: Elena, director of solutions, i'll own the integration side and joint proofs
00:20 Priya Kulkarni: Priya, se at Redwood, i'll be running the benchmark and tech deep dive if that works
00:27 Alex Chen: sweet ok high level — Verdant, we know you folks have custom hardware configs and some unique density profiles, curious what your partner motion is, reseller or more of a referral / integration play?
00:38 Marco Diaz: good question, right now we run a mix — channel led for large enterprise, referral for smaller, and we're trying to find partners to enable private deployments for customers who want on-prem or vpc. so both -- reseller and integration possible, depends on config and margin.
00:55 Ravi Singh: and we have a few customers asking for turnkey private deployments with KMS integration, HSM options and strict audit logs, so the compliance story matters.
01:05 Alex Chen: yeah that's consistent with what we see. Redwood has three modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments with a customer-controlled control plane. For partners, we've done both reseller (we bill, you operate) and referral (you bill, we do tech support) models.
01:20 Elena Park: when you say private deployments can you clarify network model? is it full VPC peering, or do you offer an on-site package?
01:28 Priya Kulkarni: good question — we support VPC connectors for cloud partners (we can peer into your VPC or you can host our private control plane). we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped installs, but that tends to be a multi-week on-boarding. for the peering case we need network egress rules, and we can support customer KMS via KMIP/HSM or cloud KMS integrations.
01:46 Marco Diaz: ok so for a co-managed flow we'd likely want the peering option. cost split and SLAs are the negotiable bits.
01:54 Alex Chen: yep. on SLAs, Redwood offers SLA-backed latency and uptime for Dedicated contracts; for private deployments SLA terms are typically part of the enterprise agreement. most partners choose to surface Redwood SLAs in their sales materials.
02:06 Ravi Singh: curious about quantization and SKU support — we run A100, H100 and our new VesperX64 boards, do you have guidance on model quantization compatibility?
02:17 Priya Kulkarni: we do. runtime handles FP16, BF16 and int8-like quantization profiles — performance/quality tradeoffs depend on model and kernels. for H100 we use tensor core optimized kernels and see 2-3x throughput improvement on typical transformer loads. with custom boards like VesperX64 we'll need to validate kernel compatibility; that's part of the benchmark.
02:36 Elena Park: and for things like KV cache / continuous batching — does your runtime support caching across requests if customers want to pin sessions?
02:42 Priya Kulkarni: yes runtime includes KV cache management and smart caching; we can expose configs to tune TTLs and prefix caching. caveat — some caching modes are less available in our hosted multi-tenant offering for security, but on Dedicated or Private you get full control.
02:58 Marco Diaz: great. what's the typical lead time to get a dedicated pool on Redwood? we hear customers asking for predictable capacity.
03:05 Alex Chen: for Dedicated it's usually 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and contracts; for Private deployments it's longer — 4-12 weeks for the on-prem variant due to install and compliance checks.
03:16 Marco Diaz: understood. one of the things we'd like is a clear benchmark we can run to show perf on our infra vs public clouds for sales plays. can Redwood run a bench against our hardware?
03:25 Priya Kulkarni: yes that's exactly what we do in partner onboarding. we'll need sample models, expected seq lengths, tokens/sec targets and a datasheet of the GPU SKUs. we'll coordinate a test harness — usually it's a perf run with a mixture of generation + embeddings and a few convo chat patterns.
03:41 Alex Chen: rough timeline — we can do an initial perf run in 2 weeks after we have artifacts; deeper kernel validation in 4 weeks. does that align with Verdant timelines?
03:49 Marco Diaz: sounds reasonable. our go-to-market push is early q1 2027 so getting benchmarks done in december would help.
03:57 Elena Park: from the security side, customers ask for SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML and audit logs — what's Redwood's posture?
04:05 Priya Kulkarni: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant, we have ISO efforts in flight — for private deployments we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and integration with customer KMS for encryption at rest. we can share our security pack; note the auto-transcription might garble some acronyms, but we'll send the security whitepaper.
04:24 Ravi Singh: in the event a customer needs encryption keys in HSM, do you support HSM-backed keys?
04:28 Priya Kulkarni: yes we support HSM/KMS via standard integrations; for private installs we can integrate on-prem HSMs via KMIP.
04:35 Marco Diaz: pricing and commercials — are you proposing a revenue share for reseller or a referral fee?
04:41 Alex Chen: typically for reseller it's a margin split — depends on committed capacity; for referral it's a fixed referral fee plus support credits. we can share a simple pricing framework in the partner deck.
04:52 Marco Diaz: ok if you can share the deck and an example commerical term sheet that would speed internal okays.
04:57 Alex Chen: yep will do.
05:00 Elena Park: one more technical question, do you support multi-tenant isolation at the model level? some customers want strict tenant isolation per model instance.
05:06 Priya Kulkarni: on Dedicated and Private you can pin model instances to isolated GPU pools; multi-tenant in hosted is logical isolation with RBAC and token scoping but not physical separation. we'll document the security tradeoffs in the PRD we share.
05:22 Marco Diaz: excellent. next steps i'm hearing: partner deck + pricing, benchmark spec, region/capacity doc from Verdant, and schedule tech deep dive.
05:30 Alex Chen: correct -- Alex will send deck, Priya will own tech scheduling, Marco to share infra doc. we should pick dates now?
05:36 Marco Diaz: how's 12/7 for the tech deep dive?
05:38 Priya Kulkarni: 12/7 16:00 UTC works for me, i'll block it and send calendar invite.
05:43 Elena Park: i'll invite our channel lead as well.
05:46 Alex Chen: perfect. any open risks or blockers?
05:49 Marco Diaz: only blocker is internal capacity verification on our side — we'll confirm by 12/3. also need clarity on co-marketing alignment.
05:58 Alex Chen: fair. we'll include a co-marketing section in the deck.
06:02 Ravi Singh: small nit — some of your docs previously said "Redwood Dedicated" but our internal notes had "Redwood Dedicated Pool" spelled differently, minor naming mismatch that confuses legal.
06:12 Alex Chen: good catch, we'll standardize naming in the deck and legal term sheet.
06:17 Marco Diaz: thanks everyone, that's it from me.
06:20 Alex Chen: awesome thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
06:24 End of recording.
